instruction.text: Select the image of the volcano.

feedback.finish: A volcano is a vent in the Earth’s crust that can erupt to release molten rock, hot gases and rock fragments.

instruction.text: Label the remaining parts of the volcano.

atoms.b: The main body of a ((tsunami ++volcano)) is called the cone. It is made of layers of cooled lava and ash.
The magma chamber holds the volcano’s magma supply. During an ((operation ++eruption)), the magma travels up the main vent before it erupts out of the ((++crater cloud)).
Sometimes, a secondary vent will form. This is a small opening in the side of the volcano that ((grass ++lava)) will flow out of if there is a blockage elsewhere.
Eruption clouds consist of ((water ++gas)) and ash that are thrown into the air.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Volcanoes are usually found at the point where two tectonic plates meet, which is called a plate boundary. There are two types of plate boundary that volcanoes can be found at.
The first is a destructive plate boundary. Here, oceanic plates are forced underneath continental ones and melt. The magma created then rises back to the Earth’s surface and creates a volcano.
The second is a constructive plate boundary. As two plates move away from each other, the gap created fills with magma. This magma rises up to form a volcano.

b: in the middle of a tectonic plate
